scenes.sub: India's retail inflation crosses the RBI's 6% limit
scenes.narration: Yesterday at four in the evening, a number came out that every economist in India was waiting for.
Retail inflation jumped to six point zero nine percent in October. For the first time in two years, it crossed the RBI's upper limit.
Within minutes, phones lit up across the country. And the big question was simple. Why is everything getting more expensive?

scenes.label: FOOD INFLATION %
scenes.note: Vegetable prices pushed the number up
scenes.narration: The main reason is food. Heavy rains damaged crops, so fewer vegetables reached the market, and prices climbed month after month.
